content.text: Hi

:  thanks for the bug report.  Can you specify the precise steps you took to reproduce the issue.  Please include the docker command you used to bring up the container and the curl commands you made in the order you made them.   That will help us troubleshoot.
I use the default docker image/start command with the following additions:

FROM fcrepo/fcrepo:6.2.0

RUN mkdir -p /etc/fin
COPY fcrepo.properties /etc/fin/fcrepo.properties
COPY root-authorization.ttl /etc/fin/root-authorization.ttl

COPY tomcat-users.xml $CATALINA_HOME/conf/tomcat-users.xml
ENV FEDORA_USER_USERNAME=fedoraUser
ENV FEDORA_USER_PASSWORD=fedoraUser

COPY activemq.xml $CATALINA_HOME/webapps/fcrepo/WEB-INF/classes/activemq.xml

ENV CATALINA_OPTS="-Dfcrepo.config.file=/etc/fin/fcrepo.properties"
Running via a docker compose file with the following mount:

volumes:
      - fedora-data:/usr/local/tomcat/fcrepo-home/data
How I create/delete this example container:

I have a wrapper CLI (node) that uses a POST command to create the container with a SLUG header wrapped in a transaction.  The transaction is rolled back if the container fails to be created at the requested slug.
Create Commands:
POST to /fcr:tx
POST to path with slug header.
Either PUT to /fcr:tx/[id] or DELETE /fcr:tx/[id] depending if the POST was created at requested path
Delete Commands
DELETE path/to/container
DELETE path/to/container/fcr:tombstone

I was trying to migrate to the PUT command instead of the POST command to create LDP containers, when the POST command stoped returning the request slug in the path.  When I tried the PUT command via curl, the 404 was returned.
Hi Justin,
I’ve been trying to reproduce this using both the POST with the slug header and a PUT to the container id but have not been successful. Here’s what I’ve tried:
Created a Dockerfile in a similar nature to yours (minus the root-auth and activemq config) + docker compose file for connecting to a postgres db
Created a minimal fcrepo.properties specifying fcrepo.home and fcrepo.db configuration properties
Start up docker
Create an initial
collection
container
Execute the following (roughly):

tx=$(curl -s -I -X POST -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/fcr:tx | grep Link | cut -c 8-84)
curl -H "Atomic-ID: ${tx}" -H "Slug: ex1-pets" -X POST -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/
curl -X PUT -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" ${tx}
curl -I -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets

curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets
curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets/fcr:tombstone
I have these running in a loop so that I can break if I get a non-200 back from the POST or GET. For the PUT I remove the Slug header and add
ex1-pets
to the url. I also tried building the one-click jar and was able to run without seeing any errant 404s.

I’m trying to think of anything else to try to see if I’ve missed something while trying to replicate this. Potentially something with the activemq config if anything was changed there? Though I’m not sure how that could impact it, but I want to make sure I haven’t overlooked anything.

Thanks for looking into this.  It seems to happen sporadically, every 1-2 days of development adding/removing same collection.  Let me see if I can come up with a script that reliably reproduces issue for you and send it over.

So this bug is proving very hard to reproduce in a reliably scriptable manor.  I have my wrapper cli writing HTTP requests as curl commands for debugging here.  The summary of what’s happening here is;
create collection (with child containers)
kill (ctrl+c) in middle of script (while transaction is open)
delete collection root container (and tombstone), both commands fail, expected.
create collection (dies on container with open transaction, expected)

comments.body: Hi Justin Merz : thanks for the bug report. Can you specify the precise steps you took to reproduce the issue. Please include the docker command you used to bring up the container and the curl commands you made in the order you made them. That will help us troubleshoot.

I use the default docker image/start command with the following additions:

FROM fcrepo/fcrepo:6.2.0

RUN mkdir -p /etc/fin
COPY fcrepo.properties /etc/fin/fcrepo.properties
COPY root-authorization.ttl /etc/fin/root-authorization.ttl

COPY tomcat-users.xml $CATALINA_HOME/conf/tomcat-users.xml
ENV FEDORA_USER_USERNAME=fedoraUser
ENV FEDORA_USER_PASSWORD=fedoraUser

COPY activemq.xml $CATALINA_HOME/webapps/fcrepo/WEB-INF/classes/activemq.xml

ENV CATALINA_OPTS="-Dfcrepo.config.file=/etc/fin/fcrepo.properties"

Running via a docker compose file with the following mount:

    volumes:
      - fedora-data:/usr/local/tomcat/fcrepo-home/data

How I create/delete this example container:

I have a wrapper CLI (node) that uses a POST command to create the container with a SLUG header wrapped in a transaction. The transaction is rolled back if the container fails to be created at the requested slug.

Create Commands:

  • POST to /fcr:tx
  • POST to path with slug header.
  • Either PUT to /fcr:tx/[id] or DELETE /fcr:tx/[id] depending if the POST was created at requested path

Delete Commands

  • DELETE path/to/container
  • DELETE path/to/container/fcr:tombstone

I was trying to migrate to the PUT command instead of the POST command to create LDP containers, when the POST command stoped returning the request slug in the path. When I tried the PUT command via curl, the 404 was returned.

Hi Justin,
I’ve been trying to reproduce this using both the POST with the slug header and a PUT to the container id but have not been successful. Here’s what I’ve tried:

  1. Created a Dockerfile in a similar nature to yours (minus the root-auth and activemq config) + docker compose file for connecting to a postgres db
  2. Created a minimal fcrepo.properties specifying fcrepo.home and fcrepo.db configuration properties
  3. Start up docker
  4. Create an initial collection container
  5. Execute the following (roughly):
tx=$(curl -s -I -X POST -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/fcr:tx | grep Link | cut -c 8-84)
curl -H "Atomic-ID: ${tx}" -H "Slug: ex1-pets" -X POST -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/
curl -X PUT -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" ${tx}
curl -I -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets

curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets
curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -u "fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/ex1-pets/fcr:tombstone

I have these running in a loop so that I can break if I get a non-200 back from the POST or GET. For the PUT I remove the Slug header and add ex1-pets to the url. I also tried building the one-click jar and was able to run without seeing any errant 404s.

I’m trying to think of anything else to try to see if I’ve missed something while trying to replicate this. Potentially something with the activemq config if anything was changed there? Though I’m not sure how that could impact it, but I want to make sure I haven’t overlooked anything.

Thanks for looking into this. It seems to happen sporadically, every 1-2 days of development adding/removing same collection. Let me see if I can come up with a script that reliably reproduces issue for you and send it over.

So this bug is proving very hard to reproduce in a reliably scriptable manor. I have my wrapper cli writing HTTP requests as curl commands for debugging here. The summary of what’s happening here is;

  • delete collection root container (and tombstone), both commands fail, expected.
